firefighter-killed-in-brooklyn-blaze-hon.title: Firefighter Who Died at Brooklyn Fire Honored at FDNY Memorial
firefighter-killed-in-brooklyn-blaze-hon.dek: Lt. Patrick Brady of Ladder 120 was one of 11 FDNY members whose names were added Wednesday to the department's Upper Manhattan memorial.
body: Wednesday, Riverside Drive. FDNY Lt. Patrick Brady's name was added to the department's memorial, amNY reported. Brady died after a medical emergency while working a Brooklyn fire last year.

The ceremony is held every year at the Firemen's Memorial at West 100th Street and Riverside Drive. This year it added the names of 11 active or retired members who died over the past year, according to amNY. Thousands of firefighters attended. So did Fire Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore and Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Brady served with Ladder Company 120. On Nov. 8, 2025, he suffered a medical episode on a roof at 9407 Kings Highway, amNY reported. He went into cardiac arrest. He could not be revived. He joined the FDNY in 2014 and served at Engine 227. He transferred to Ladder 120 in 2022.

Mamdani presented Brady's widow with the FDNY flag, according to amNY. The commissioner presented the department's medal of valor. Ladder 120 commander Chris Hagen described Brady as a skilled firefighter and a good teacher to younger members. Mamdani noted that nearly 1,200 FDNY members have died in service to the city.
Paramedic Salih Abdur Rahman was also honored. He died on Oct. 29, 2025, after finishing a shift at the FDNY Training Academy on Randall's Island.

queens-student-arrested-after-bringing-g.title: Queens Student, 15, Taken Into Custody After Gun Found in Backpack
queens-student-arrested-after-bringing-g.dek: A staff member at a Queens Village high school campus spotted a handgun in a 15-year-old's backpack after a fight, amNY reported. He was detained.
body: Just after 1 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 7, police were called to 230-17 Hillside Avenue in Queens Village. A 15-year-old student was taken into custody there after a handgun was found in his backpack, according to police sources cited by amNY.
The building houses Martin Van Buren High School and Business Technology Early College High School, the outlet reported. Officers from the 105th Precinct responded.
Two boys had gotten into a fight inside the building, according to police sources. Afterward, a staff member spotted a 9mm handgun in one of the boys' backpacks, the report said.
School Safety agents held the student until police arrived, according to amNY.

Charges were pending the outcome of an ongoing investigation, law enforcement sources told the outlet. Neither student was identified. The article did not say whether anyone was hurt in the fight. It did not say what happened to the second boy.

nyc-crime-hits-historic-lows-through-nin.title: NYC Crime Hits Historic Lows Through Nine Months, but Hate Crimes Rise
nyc-crime-hits-historic-lows-through-nin.dek: NYPD figures show major crime and murders down through September. Reported hate crimes rose nearly 13 percent.
body: Major crime in New York City fell 9.4% in the third quarter from a year earlier, according to NYPD data reported by NY1. Murders drove the drop. They fell 19.8%, from 91 to 73. Reported hate crimes rose.

July 1 to Sept. 30: car thefts down 17.1%. Robberies down 13.6%. Burglaries down 11.7%. Grand larcenies down 10.2%, NY1 reported. Shooting incidents fell 22.7%. Year to date, major crime is down 6.6%. Murders fell from 253 to 203.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch spoke at a briefing. She said the first nine months and the third quarter had the fewest shootings, shooting victims and murders on record for the five boroughs. She credited the department's precision policing strategy, including removing illegal guns and dismantling gangs, according to NY1.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said September set record lows for shootings. He said work remains. He named hate crimes as a key concern. Hate crimes rose 12.6% in the quarter and 12.9% year to date, NY1 reported.

Anti-Jewish incidents made up 52.9% of confirmed hate crimes through September. There were 245, compared with 242 a year earlier. In the third quarter alone they fell 13.2%. Anti-Muslim hate crimes rose from 18 to 32 year to date, according to NY1.

ex-midtown-attorney-faces-more-charges-i.title: Former Midtown Attorney Faces New Charges in Sexual Assault Case
ex-midtown-attorney-faces-more-charges-i.dek: Manhattan prosecutors accused Ryan Hemphill, a former attorney, of sexually assaulting a seventh woman in his Midtown apartment, amNY reported.
body: Tuesday, Oct. 6. Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg announced new charges against Ryan Hemphill, according to amNY. Hemphill, 44, is a former attorney. He is accused of sexually assaulting a seventh woman in his Midtown apartment.
Prosecutors allege the newly charged assault took place in spring 2024. They say it lasted about seven hours, the outlet reported. Hemphill returned to court on Oct. 6.

Hemphill was indicted in 2025. That indictment accused him of assaulting six women between October 2024 and March 2025, according to the report. The current indictment in state Supreme Court has 41 counts. They include nine counts of predatory sexual assault, multiple rape counts, first-degree aggravated sexual assault and second-degree assault, among other charges.

Hemphill met the woman through a dating website, according to court documents cited by amNY. Prosecutors also allege he pressured victims into recording statements saying the encounters were consensual.

Bragg called the alleged conduct horrific, the outlet reported. He thanked the woman for coming forward. He said she did so after learning of the earlier allegations. He said the investigation is continuing. Anyone with information can call his office at 212-335-3400.
Hemphill has been held without bail since the 2025 indictment, according to amNY. He remains in jail awaiting trial. The charges are accusations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

bronx-man-dies-of-stab-wounds-as-woman-t.title: Man Fatally Stabbed in Fordham After Argument; Suspect Sought
bronx-man-dies-of-stab-wounds-as-woman-t.dek: A man believed to be in his 20s was stabbed in the back near Walton Avenue and East Fordham Road. A nearby worker tried to help him. He died, amNY reported.
body: Just before 10:30 a.m. Monday, Oct. 5. Walton Avenue and East Fordham Road, in the Fordham section of the Bronx. A man believed to be in his 20s was stabbed, according to police sources cited by amNY. He died.

Officers from the 46th Precinct answered a 911 call. They found the man with a stab wound to his back, police said. Several witnesses told first responders they had seen two men arguing just before the attack, the outlet reported.

A worker at a nearby training center told amNY she saw the man run down the block. He collapsed outside an entrance. She said she pressed on his wound until an ambulance arrived. She said he asked her not to let him die. She said EMS asked whether he knew who stabbed him. He said yes, she said.
EMS took him to St. Barnabas Hospital. He was pronounced dead there, according to the report. Police withheld his name pending family notification.

Police are looking for a man also believed to be in his 20s. He argued with the victim moments before the stabbing. He was last seen in all black, running north on Morris Avenue, police said. No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing. Tips go to Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

bronx-woman-dies-after-being-found-with-.title: Police Investigate Death of Woman Found Injured in Melrose Apartment Building
bronx-woman-dies-after-being-found-with-.dek: A 35-year-old woman was found with injuries to her head, face and body inside her Melrose building. She died at Lincoln Hospital. Police were investigating, amNY reported.
body: 370 East 158th Street, Melrose, the Bronx. A 35-year-old woman was found inside her apartment building with injuries to her head, face and body, according to amNY. Police are investigating her death.
EMS responded just before 6:30 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, law enforcement sources told the outlet. A 911 caller had reported a woman in need of assistance.
She was taken to Lincoln Hospital in critical condition. She died early Monday, Oct. 5, according to the report.

The case was reported to the 40th Precinct. Her body went to the city Medical Examiner's office for an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death, police said. The article did not say whether the death had been ruled a homicide.

No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, according to police. The report did not describe a suspect. It did not say how the woman may have been injured. Anyone with information can contact NYPD Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

hit-and-run-driver-sought-after-brooklyn.title: Driver Flees After Fatal Chain-Reaction Crash on Ocean Parkway in Midwood
hit-and-run-driver-sought-after-brooklyn.dek: An Audi struck a car on Ocean Parkway. The 62-year-old driver was killed and his passenger seriously hurt. Police were searching for the Audi's driver, amNY reported.
body: About 12:10 a.m. Monday, Oct. 5. Ocean Parkway and Avenue S, Midwood, Brooklyn. Three vehicles crashed. A 62-year-old man was killed and a 39-year-old woman seriously injured, according to police sources cited by amNY. Police were searching for a driver who fled.

Officers from the 61st Precinct responded, police said. Investigators learned that a 2026 Audi A5 heading south on Ocean Parkway struck the rear of a 2023 Toyota Camry. The 62-year-old man was driving the Camry.

The Camry spun out and hit a Toyota RAV4, according to police. The Camry and the Audi then struck trees. The Camry driver died at Maimonides Medical Center. His name was withheld pending family notification.

His 39-year-old passenger was in the rear seat. She suffered neck and back injuries, the outlet reported. The article gave conflicting accounts of her condition, describing it as both critical and stable. The 25-year-old RAV4 driver was treated at the scene for minor injuries.

The Audi's driver abandoned the wrecked car, removed its license plates and fled, police sources said. No arrests had been made. The NYPD Highway District's Collision Investigation Squad was investigating. Tips go to Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

bronx-man-charged-with-murder-in-random-.title: Bronx Man Charged With Murder in Random J Train Stabbing
bronx-man-charged-with-murder-in-random-.dek: Queens prosecutors charged a 25-year-old Bronx man with murder. They accuse him of fatally stabbing a 59-year-old passenger he did not know aboard a J train near Woodhaven Boulevard.
body: A 25-year-old Bronx man has been arraigned on a second-degree murder charge, according to the office of Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz. The charge is in the fatal stabbing of a 59-year-old man aboard a Queens-bound J train.

Prosecutors identified him as Jyrell Thomas. According to the charges, he boarded the train at Broadway Junction in Brooklyn at about 5 p.m. on Sept. 30. At about 5:15 p.m. the train approached the elevated Woodhaven Boulevard station near Jamaica Avenue. He allegedly yelled, pulled out a knife and repeatedly stabbed the man, the DA's office said. He did not know the man.

The doors opened. Thomas allegedly ran and dropped his weapon, prosecutors said. Passengers chased him. NYPD officers responding to 911 calls arrested him two blocks away, where he had climbed onto a garage. Police recovered two kitchen knives, according to the release. The victim was taken to a hospital and pronounced dead.
Katz said New Yorkers deserve to ride transit without fear, according to the release. She thanked the passengers who pursued the attacker and the officers who made the arrest.

Thomas also faces two counts of fourth-degree criminal possession of a weapon. Queens Criminal Court Judge Indira D. Khan ordered him held. The return date was Oct. 6. If convicted, he faces up to 25 years to life in prison. The charges are accusations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

man-sought-for-slashing-13-year-old-boy-.title: Police Seek Man Who Slashed 13-Year-Old Boy Outside Elmhurst Mall
man-sought-for-slashing-13-year-old-boy-.dek: Detectives released images of a man they say cut a 13-year-old boy across the face outside Queens Place Mall on Sept. 3, amNY reported.
body: Queens Place Mall, 88-01 Queens Boulevard, Elmhurst. A man slashed a 13-year-old boy across the face outside, according to amNY. Police are searching for him.

It happened at about 6:30 p.m. on Sept. 3, police said. The boy and a friend had argued with the man, according to police sources cited by the outlet. The man chased them. When he caught up, he pulled out a sharp object, cut the boy's face and ran.
Officers from the 110th Precinct and paramedics responded. EMS took the boy to Harlem Hospital. He was treated for a laceration and listed in stable condition, the report said.
Detectives released images of the suspect and asked the public to help identify him. He was last seen in a black T-shirt with red lettering, camouflage pants and a baseball cap, police said.
No arrests had been made as of the report. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit a tip at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

passenger-killed-in-apparent-dwi-crash-o.title: Passenger Killed in Suspected DWI Crash on Grand Central Parkway
passenger-killed-in-apparent-dwi-crash-o.dek: A car flipped on the Grand Central Parkway in Queens. A 23-year-old woman was thrown out and killed. The driver was taken into custody, amNY reported.
body: Early Sunday, Oct. 4. Grand Central Parkway, beneath the Steinway Overpass in Queens. A car crashed and flipped. A 23-year-old woman riding in it was killed, according to police sources cited by amNY.

It was just after 4 a.m., police said. A 34-year-old man was driving a Honda Accord west in the right lane. He swerved into the left lane and struck the left-side barrier, according to police. Then he hit a light pole. The car overturned onto its roof.
The woman was seated in the back. She was thrown from the car onto the roadway, the outlet reported. EMS took her to Elmhurst Hospital. She was pronounced dead there.

Police took the driver into custody at the scene. No charges had been filed as of the report. Sources familiar with the investigation told amNY he was believed to have been under the influence and was expected to be charged. He has not been convicted of any crime. He is presumed innocent.
The NYPD Highway District Collision Investigation Squad was still investigating, according to the report.

two-men-beaten-with-hammer-outside-brook.title: Two Men Attacked With Hammers in Dyker Heights Burger King Parking Lot
two-men-beaten-with-hammer-outside-brook.dek: Two 36-year-old men were pulled from their car outside a Dyker Heights Burger King on Saturday night and struck with hammers, amNY reported.
body: Just after 9 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 3. A Burger King parking lot at 65th Street and 14th Avenue, Dyker Heights, Brooklyn. Two 36-year-old men were attacked with hammers, according to police sources cited by amNY.
The men were sitting in their vehicle. Two unidentified men opened the car doors, pulled them out and struck them in the head with hammers, police said. Both suffered cuts, the outlet reported.
The two men got themselves to NYU Langone Hospital-Brooklyn. They were listed in stable condition, according to the report.
The attackers were described only as wearing black sweatshirts. They were last seen running north on 14th Avenue, police said.

Police had not identified a motive at the time of publication. No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, amNY reported. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit a tip at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

man-stabbed-after-argument-on-prospect-a.title: Police Seek Man Who Stabbed Another After Argument on Prospect Avenue
man-stabbed-after-argument-on-prospect-a.dek: A man was stabbed once in the torso after an argument near 2000 Prospect Avenue in the Bronx on Sept. 25. Police are asking for help identifying the attacker, Hoodline reported.
body: Near 2000 Prospect Avenue, the Bronx. A man stabbed another man after an argument. Police are asking the public to help identify him, according to Hoodline, citing News 12 Bronx.
It happened at about 9 a.m. on Sept. 25, News 12 Bronx reported. By that account, the attacker approached the victim after an argument. He stabbed him and ran off on foot.
The man was stabbed once in the left side of his torso, the reports said. EMS took him to St. Barnabas Hospital. He was in stable condition. His age was not given.
News 12 Bronx described the suspect as a man in his 40s with a dark complexion and a thin build. He was last seen in a gray hooded long-sleeve shirt and eyeglasses.

No arrest had been announced. The suspect had not been identified, according to Hoodline. The outlet noted earlier, separate stabbings on Prospect Avenue. One was an unprovoked attack in May 2025 that left a 56-year-old man critically injured, as reported by amNY. The NYPD asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS or submit tips online, where they are kept confidential.

man-29-fatally-stabbed-outside-jamaica-a.title: Man, 29, Fatally Stabbed Outside Jamaica Avenue Nightclub
man-29-fatally-stabbed-outside-jamaica-a.dek: A 29-year-old man was stabbed to death after a dispute outside a Jamaica nightclub early Saturday. Detectives were searching for the attacker, amNY reported.
body: Just before 1 a.m. Saturday, Oct. 3. Outside Seduction Restaurant and Bar, 173-12 Jamaica Avenue, Jamaica, Queens. A 29-year-old man was fatally stabbed, according to police cited by amNY.

Officers from the 103rd Precinct answered a 911 call. They found the man with multiple stab wounds to the chest, police said. EMS took him to Jamaica Hospital. He was pronounced dead a short time later. His name was withheld pending family notification.
Moments before the attack, the man had a dispute with the suspect in front of the nightclub, sources close to the case told the outlet. The cause of the dispute was not known.

The suspect is a slim man, according to sources familiar with the case. He was last seen in a black skullcap, a gold chain, a blue T-shirt, navy sweatpants with white stripes and white sneakers. He fled on foot in an unknown direction.

No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, police said. Through Sept. 27, the 103rd Precinct had recorded two homicides this year, according to NYPD figures cited by amNY. That was half the number at the same point in 2025. Tips go to Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

off-duty-nypd-detective-stabbed-in-attem.title: Off-Duty NYPD Detective Stabbed in Attempted Robbery in Norwood
off-duty-nypd-detective-stabbed-in-attem.dek: Two men tried to take an off-duty detective's chain near Rochambeau Avenue in the Bronx. He was stabbed multiple times, according to sources cited by amNY.
body: Just before 2 p.m. Friday, Oct. 2. Near 3174 Rochambeau Avenue, in the Norwood section of the Bronx. An off-duty NYPD detective was stabbed several times during an attempted robbery, according to authorities cited by amNY.

The detective is assigned to the 44th Precinct, sources familiar with the case told the outlet. He was walking to his car. Two men approached and tried to take his chain. The confrontation turned violent. He suffered at least seven stab wounds, the sources said. The two men fled on a scooter. Police had not confirmed those details in the article.
The detective was taken to Jacobi Hospital. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement that the detective was in stable condition. He described the statement as based on preliminary information.

Mamdani said he and Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch visited the detective and his family at the hospital, amNY reported. He said he was confident the NYPD would identify and arrest the suspects. The department canceled a 3 p.m. briefing at One Police Plaza. The two had been scheduled to discuss quarterly crime statistics there.
No arrests had been reported at the time of publication. The investigation was continuing, according to the outlet. The incident occurred within the 52nd Precinct.

bronx-man-found-stabbed-to-death-in-his-.title: Man Found Stabbed to Death in Belmont Home During Wellness Check
bronx-man-found-stabbed-to-death-in-his-.dek: Police on a wellness check found a 37-year-old man dead with multiple stab wounds in his Adams Place home in Belmont, amNY reported.
body: Thursday afternoon, Oct. 1. 2216 Adams Place, in the Belmont section of the Bronx. A 37-year-old man was found stabbed to death inside his home, according to law enforcement sources cited by amNY.

Officers from the 48th Precinct went to the residence at about 2:45 p.m. for a wellness check, police said. The man's fiancée had called 911 after not hearing from him for several days, sources told the outlet.
Officers found him unresponsive on the kitchen floor, according to sources. He had multiple stab wounds to his torso, left arm, left hand and back. EMS pronounced him dead at the scene.
As of Friday, Oct. 2, no arrests had been made, police said. Investigators had not determined a motive. They had not released a description of a suspect.

Through Sept. 27, the 48th Precinct had recorded three homicides this year, according to NYPD statistics cited by amNY. At the same point in 2025 it had 12. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS or message @NYPDTips on X.

man-stabbed-multiple-times-on-the-upper-.title: Man Stabbed on West 109th Street; Brooklyn Man Charged With Assault
man-stabbed-multiple-times-on-the-upper-.dek: A 44-year-old man was stabbed in the neck and back on West 109th Street. Police later arrested a 47-year-old Brooklyn man, West Side Rag reported.
body: Wednesday afternoon. 312 West 109th Street, between Riverside Drive and Broadway on the Upper West Side. A 44-year-old man was stabbed multiple times, a police spokesperson told West Side Rag.
It happened at about 1:30 p.m., police said. The man was stabbed in the neck and back. He was taken to Mount Sinai Morningside in stable condition, according to police.
A police spokesperson could not confirm whether the attack took place inside the building or on the street in front of it, the outlet reported. Police had no information about what led up to it.

On Thursday, police told West Side Rag that Jerry Pastrana, 47, of the New Lots section of Brooklyn, had been arrested in connection with the stabbing. He was charged with two counts of assault, according to police.
The article did not report a court date. It did not say whether Pastrana had entered a plea. The charges are accusations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

woman-found-stabbed-to-death-in-far-rock.title: Woman Found Stabbed to Death in Far Rockaway Apartment; Man in Custody
woman-found-stabbed-to-death-in-far-rock.dek: The 32-year-old man who lived in a Neilson Street apartment fell from the building's roof. A 31-year-old woman was then found dead inside, according to sources cited by amNY.
body: Wednesday, Sept. 30. A second-floor apartment at 10-40 Neilson Street, Far Rockaway, Queens. A 31-year-old woman was found stabbed to death inside, according to law enforcement sources cited by amNY. The 32-year-old man who lived there was in police custody.

Just before noon, a 911 caller reported a man standing on the roof of the seven-story building, sources said. Officers from the 101st Precinct responded and tried to talk with him. He jumped from the building, according to sources. He was taken to a nearby hospital in critical condition.

Investigators then entered his apartment with help from the building superintendent, the outlet reported. They found the woman unresponsive with multiple stab wounds. EMS pronounced her dead at the scene.
Investigators believe the man stabbed the woman before going to the roof, sources told amNY. The relationship between the two was not clear. The man was not named.

As of Thursday morning, Oct. 1, no charges had been filed, according to the report. The investigation was continuing. The man has not been charged with any crime and is presumed innocent. Anyone with information was asked to contact Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

bronx-motorcyclist-badly-hurt-driver-arr.title: Motorcyclist Critically Hurt in Bronx Crash; Driver Charged With DWI
bronx-motorcyclist-badly-hurt-driver-arr.dek: A 42-year-old motorcyclist was critically injured in a multi-vehicle crash at Crotona Avenue and East 189th Street. Police charged another driver with driving while intoxicated, amNY reported.
body: About 8:40 p.m. Sept. 30. Crotona Avenue and East 189th Street, the Bronx. A 42-year-old motorcyclist was critically injured in a multi-vehicle crash, according to amNY. Police arrested another driver on DWI charges.

The man was riding a 2014 Kawasaki Ninja south on Crotona Avenue, police said. He lost control and struck the rear of a 2015 Ford Taurus. The impact sent him into the northbound lane. There he collided head-on with a 2007 Cadillac DTS driven by a 46-year-old man, police said. The motorcycle then hit a parked car.

Officers from the 48th Precinct found the motorcyclist with serious head and body injuries. EMS took him to St. Barnabas Hospital. He remained in critical condition Thursday morning, the outlet reported. The 30-year-old Taurus driver and his 30-year-old passenger were taken to a hospital for observation.

Police identified the Cadillac's driver as Carless Currie of Parkchester. He stayed at the scene. He allegedly refused a breathalyzer test, according to the report. Police later determined he was intoxicated and did not have a valid license. He was charged with driving while intoxicated, aggravated unlicensed operation and refusing a test, among other counts.
The NYPD Highway Patrol Collision Investigation Squad is still investigating. The charges are accusations. Currie is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

police-seek-attacker-who-punched-72-year.title: Police Seek Man Who Punched 72-Year-Old in Unprovoked Parkchester Attack
police-seek-attacker-who-punched-72-year.dek: Detectives released surveillance images of a man police say punched a 72-year-old man in the face outside a Parkchester pharmacy on Sept. 15, amNY reported.
body: Outside a pharmacy at 1320 Metropolitan Avenue, Parkchester, the Bronx. A man punched a 72-year-old man in the face in an unprovoked attack, police say, according to amNY. Police are searching for him.

It happened at about 1:30 p.m. on Sept. 15, police said. The older man was walking on the sidewalk. The assailant rushed up to him without saying anything and struck him on the right side of his face, according to police.
The man fell to the ground and cut his knees. He had pain and swelling to his face, the outlet reported. EMS treated him at the scene. He declined further medical attention.
The attacker fled on foot. He was last seen in a blue hat, a jacket and brown jeans, police said. Detectives released surveillance images and asked the public to help identify him.

No arrest had been reported as of publication, according to amNY. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit a tip at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

suspect-in-top-hat-sought-in-stabbing-of.title: Three Men Stabbed at Bowery and Delancey; Suspect in Top Hat Sought
suspect-in-top-hat-sought-in-stabbing-of.dek: Police say a man stabbed three men at Bowery and Delancey Street after an argument over food, then took one victim's fanny pack. He is being sought, amNY reported.
body: About 1:10 a.m. Wednesday, Sept. 30. Bowery and Delancey Street, the Lower East Side. Three men were stabbed, according to law enforcement sources cited by amNY. Detectives were searching for the attacker.

The suspect began arguing with a 26-year-old man over food the man was eating, according to the outlet. The suspect allegedly pulled out a sharp object and stabbed him. Then he allegedly attacked two other men who tried to intervene. The 26-year-old told police he did not know his attacker.

Officers from the 5th Precinct found the three men wounded at the scene. The 26-year-old was stabbed in the stomach. A 21-year-old was stabbed in the left shoulder. A 19-year-old was stabbed in the left arm, police said. EMS took all three to Bellevue Hospital. Their injuries were not considered life-threatening.
During the attack the suspect allegedly took the 26-year-old's fanny pack, the report said. It held his keys, credit cards and identification.

Police described the suspect as a man in his 40s with dreadlocks. He wore a top hat, a dark sweatshirt with white stripes on the sides, dark gloves and blue jeans. The hat fell off as he ran north on the Bowery, according to amNY. No arrests had been reported. Tips go to Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

man-stabbed-in-back-and-torso-in-morrisa.title: Man Stabbed Multiple Times Inside Morrisania Apartment After Argument
man-stabbed-in-back-and-torso-in-morrisa.dek: A 34-year-old man was stabbed in the back and torso during an argument inside a Union Avenue apartment in the Bronx. The attacker fled, amNY reported.
body: Tuesday night, Sept. 29. A second-floor apartment at 925 Union Avenue, in the Morrisania section of the Bronx. A 34-year-old man was stabbed multiple times, according to police and law enforcement sources cited by amNY.
Officers from the 42nd Precinct arrived just before 8:30 p.m. on a report of a person stabbed, police said. They found the man inside the apartment.

Moments before the attack, the man had a verbal argument with another man in the apartment, according to law enforcement sources. The suspect then stabbed him twice in the back and several times in the left side of his torso, the sources said. Police did not say what led to the dispute.
EMS took the man to Lincoln Hospital. He was listed in stable condition, the outlet reported.

Police described the suspect as a man dressed in all black. He was seen leaving the building shortly after the attack. As of Wednesday morning he had not been caught. No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, according to amNY. Tips go to Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

brooklyn-commuter-killed-after-bag-caugh.title: Brooklyn Commuter Killed After Bag Caught in A Train Doors
brooklyn-commuter-killed-after-bag-caugh.dek: A departing A train dragged a 57-year-old man along the platform at the Utica Avenue station. He died, police sources said.
body: Monday evening. The Utica Avenue A train station in Brooklyn. A 57-year-old man was killed after a bag he was carrying got caught in the doors of a departing train, amNY reported, citing police sources.

It was about 5:48 p.m. on Sept. 28, on the Manhattan-bound platform, according to amNY. The train began moving and dragged the man along the platform, police sources said. He had difficulty walking and used a cane. He tried to alert the conductor by hitting the doors, sources said.
The motorman did not realize what had happened until it was too late, according to a preliminary investigation cited by amNY. Police described the death as an apparent accident.
NYPD Transit District 33 and EMS responded. The man was pronounced dead shortly after 6 p.m., amNY reported. No criminality is suspected, police sources said.
The investigation is ongoing. amNY said it had asked the MTA for comment. It was awaiting a response at publication.

woman-sought-for-choking-rider-on-bronx-.title: Police Seek Woman Accused of Choking Rider Aboard Bx4 Bus in Fordham
woman-sought-for-choking-rider-on-bronx-.dek: Police released images of a woman they say punched and choked a 28-year-old rider after an argument aboard a Bx4 bus in the Bronx on Sept. 9, amNY reported.
body: A Bx4 bus in the Fordham section of the Bronx. A woman punched and choked a fellow passenger, police say, according to amNY. Police are asking for help identifying her.

It happened at about 4 p.m. on Sept. 9 as the bus approached Webster Avenue and East Fordham Road, police sources told the outlet. The 28-year-old victim had just boarded the crowded bus, law enforcement sources said. She accidentally bumped into the suspect.

They argued. The suspect allegedly grabbed the woman by the neck, punched the left side of her face and choked her, according to sources. Seconds later she got off the bus and left in an unknown direction, police said.
EMS took the victim to NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital in stable condition, sources said. Her injuries were not life-threatening. They included bruising, shoulder pain and difficulty breathing.

The incident was reported to the 52nd Precinct. Police released images of the suspect. She is believed to be 35 to 40 years old. She was last seen in a black shirt and black pants. No arrests had been made, according to amNY. Tips go to Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

woman-killed-in-hit-and-run-while-biking.title: Woman Killed in Hit-and-Run While Biking on 34th Street
woman-killed-in-hit-and-run-while-biking.dek: A dump truck struck and killed a cyclist in Midtown. The driver was later taken into custody, police said.
body: Monday morning. West 34th Street, Midtown. A dump truck struck and killed a woman riding an e-bike, amNY reported, citing police. The driver kept going.

It was just before 11 a.m. on Sept. 28, between Seventh and Eighth avenues, according to amNY. She was riding westbound on a wet street. Police first described her as a teenager. Then they said she was 51. Transportation Alternatives said she was a delivery worker. EMS pronounced her dead at the scene.

The dump truck was later found at Fifth Avenue and 35th Street, amNY reported. The driver was detained, given a sobriety test and taken into custody. No charges had been filed at publication. The sobriety test result was not reported. Officers from the Midtown South Precinct and the NYPD Collision Investigation Squad responded.

Transportation Alternatives executive director Ben Furnas said she was the 20th bike rider killed in the city this year, including 17 e-bike riders, according to amNY. He said hers was the 149th traffic death citywide this year. He criticized the lack of bike infrastructure on 34th Street. He noted a City Council hearing on e-bikes scheduled within days.
amNY described the case as a developing story. The driver's identity had not been reported. Neither had any charges.

man-charged-with-murdering-woman-in-cent.title: Man Charged With Murder After Woman Found Dead in Central Park's Ramble
man-charged-with-murdering-woman-in-cent.dek: A 63-year-old woman was found dead inside a gazebo in Central Park's Ramble. The NYPD charged a 36-year-old man with murder, NY1 reported.
body: Sunday morning, Sept. 27. A gazebo in the Ramble section of Central Park. A 63-year-old woman was found dead inside, according to the NYPD as cited by NY1. A 36-year-old man has been charged with murder.
Police identified him as Jonathan Robles. By Sunday evening he had been charged with murder and criminal possession of a weapon, the NYPD said.
Police told NY1 the woman was homeless. Her name had not been released while police searched for her next of kin, the outlet reported.

People who knew her described her to NY1 as a familiar and gentle presence in the park. One acquaintance said she had fed him over the years. He said she considered the gazebo her home. A birder said she painted and displayed her artwork in the Ramble.
Major crime in Central Park is up nearly 30% this year, officials said, according to the report. There have been 83 major felonies so far, compared with 64 at the same point last year.
NY1 did not report a court date, plea, bail status or motive. The charges are accusations. Robles is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

man-critically-wounded-after-being-shot-.title: Man Critically Wounded in Shooting Outside Brooklyn Deli
man-critically-wounded-after-being-shot-.dek: A 27-year-old man was shot in the head at a deli on Rutland Road early Monday. Police were searching for a gunman believed to have fled in a gray sedan, amNY reported.
body: Early Monday, Sept. 28. A deli at 980 Rutland Road, Brooklyn. A 27-year-old man was shot in the head and critically wounded, according to NYPD sources cited by amNY. The outlet placed the location in Brownsville.

Officers from the 67th Precinct were called at about 3:20 a.m. on reports of shots fired, police sources said. They found the man with a gunshot wound to the left side of his head, according to law enforcement sources.
EMS took him to Brookdale University Hospital. He remained in critical condition, the outlet reported.

The gunman is believed to have fled in a gray four-door sedan. Police sources did not describe him. They gave no information about what led to the shooting. The scene stayed sealed off well after sunrise as detectives searched for evidence, according to the report.

No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing. Shootings in the 67th Precinct fell 65% this year through Sept. 20, from 25 to nine, according to figures cited by amNY. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

man-dies-after-being-dropped-off-at-elmh.title: Police Investigate Death of Man Left at Elmhurst Hospital
man-dies-after-being-dropped-off-at-elmh.dek: An unidentified driver dropped a 37-year-old man off at Elmhurst Hospital in Queens. He died. Police called the circumstances suspicious, amNY reported.
body: Elmhurst Hospital, 79-01 Broadway, Queens. A 37-year-old man was dropped off there and died, according to police sources cited by amNY. Police described the circumstances as suspicious. They are investigating.
Officers from the 110th Precinct were called to the hospital just after 10:30 p.m. on Sept. 27 after the death was reported, the outlet said.

The man had been seen vomiting on a sidewalk, according to a preliminary investigation, police said. He was then placed into a Toyota Highlander driven by an unidentified person. Witnesses said the driver took him to the hospital and left him there, according to the report.
Hospital staff brought him inside. He could not be saved. He was pronounced dead. He had no visible signs of trauma, police sources said. His name was withheld pending family notification.

His body went to the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner for an autopsy to determine the cause of death. The investigation was continuing, police said. No arrests were reported. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

washington-heights-shelter-resident-char.title: Washington Heights Shelter Resident Charged in Fatal Stabbing
washington-heights-shelter-resident-char.dek: A 33-year-old man was fatally stabbed during an argument inside the Fort Washington Men's Shelter. A 29-year-old resident was charged with murder, amNY reported.
body: A 29-year-old resident of a Washington Heights homeless shelter has been charged with murder, according to police sources cited by amNY. A man was fatally stabbed during an argument inside the facility.
Just before noon, Sept. 27. The Fort Washington Men's Shelter, 651 West 168th Street, the outlet reported. Officers from the 33rd Precinct answered a 911 call reporting an argument and a stabbing.

Police found a 33-year-old man with multiple stab wounds to his chest. EMS took him to Harlem Hospital in critical condition. He later died there, according to the report. His name was withheld pending family notification.
Police identified the accused as Javed Tyghter. He was taken into custody and charged with murder, police sources said. The article did not report a court date or plea.

The facility houses 200 men dealing with mental health and substance use disorders, according to the shelter's website, amNY reported. The outlet said the killing was the first reported murder in the 33rd Precinct this year. The charges are accusations. Tyghter is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

man-charged-in-fatal-beating-of-woman-ne.title: Police Say Woman Killed Near Central Park Boathouse Was Beaten With Stick
man-charged-in-fatal-beating-of-woman-ne.dek: Detectives charged a 36-year-old man with murder in the death of a 63-year-old woman found in a gazebo near the Central Park Boathouse. They revised their account of how she died, amNY reported.
body: Sunday morning, Sept. 27. A wooden gazebo near the Boathouse in Central Park. A 63-year-old woman was found there. A 36-year-old man has been charged with murder and criminal possession of a weapon in her death, according to police cited by amNY.

She was found unconscious with a head injury at 9:43 a.m. near East 74th Street and East Drive, police said. Officers from the Central Park Precinct and EMS responded. EMS pronounced her dead at about 10 a.m. Her name was withheld pending family notification.
Police had first reported that she had stab wounds. They now say the accused beat her with a wooden stick, the outlet reported.
Detectives identified the accused as Jonathan Robles. He is homeless and has an address listed at the Barbour Hotel shelter in Hell's Kitchen, according to the report.

The woman is believed to have been homeless and living in the area, amNY reported. She had a tent and belongings near the gazebo. Sources described her as a known artist who sold her paintings there. Detectives sealed off the area and examined it in heavy rain.
The charges are accusations. Robles is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

bodycam-suggests-times-square-stabbing-s.title: NYPD Releases Bodycam Video of Fatal Times Square Police Shooting
bodycam-suggests-times-square-stabbing-s.dek: Footage released by the NYPD appears to show a woman accused of stabbing two people saying she wanted to die before officers shot her.
body: Sept. 25. The NYPD released body camera footage of the Aug. 31 fatal police shooting of a woman in Times Square, amNY reported. The video appears to show her expressing an intention to be killed by officers.

Police said the 49-year-old Queens woman stabbed two people near a subway entrance at West 43rd Street and Seventh Avenue, according to amNY. Witnesses described the attacks as unprovoked. A 32-year-old woman died at Bellevue Hospital. A 68-year-old man survived, law enforcement sources said.

About 4:25 p.m., two officers encountered the woman on Seventh Avenue near the NYPD substation, amNY reported. She still held two knives. One officer tried to talk her down, guns holstered. The footage captures her saying this was the only way out.

About 4:29 p.m., more officers arrived. Two fired Tasers. They were ineffective, according to amNY. The woman advanced toward officers with the knives. Two officers fired about three shots. She was pronounced dead at Bellevue Hospital.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the officers did what they were trained to do. The footage came out less than a month after the shooting, amid Mayor Zohran Mamdani's pledge to release police video faster. amNY reported no findings or final determinations on the shooting.

man-shot-dead-outside-queens-strip-club-.title: Man Fatally Shot Outside Astoria Club in Apparent Robbery Attempt
man-shot-dead-outside-queens-strip-club-.dek: A gunman tried to take a 45-year-old man's jewelry outside a Steinway Street club. During a struggle, the man was shot in the back, amNY reported.
body: About 3:45 a.m. Thursday, Sept. 24. Outside the Riviera Gentleman's Club, 34-48 Steinway Street, Astoria, Queens. A 45-year-old man was shot and killed, according to amNY. Police called it an apparent robbery attempt.

The gunman approached the man from behind and tried to take his jewelry, according to a preliminary investigation, police sources said. They struggled. The gunman fired. The bullet struck the man in the back, according to police.
The gunman ran, got into an SUV and drove off along 35th Avenue, police said. Investigators do not believe he took any of the man's belongings. The outlet did not report a description of him.
Officers from the 114th Precinct and EMS responded. The man was taken to Elmhurst Hospital in critical condition. He died there, the report said. His name was withheld pending family notification.

No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing. Murders in the 114th Precinct have doubled this year, from two at this point last year to four, according to NYPD data cited by amNY. Tips go to Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

two-alarm-bronx-fire-leaves-one-dead-ano.title: Two-Alarm Bronx Fire Leaves One Dead, Another Hurt After Window Jump
two-alarm-bronx-fire-leaves-one-dead-ano.dek: A fire in a six-story Montgomery Avenue apartment building killed one person. More than a dozen others were hurt, four of them firefighters.
body: About 7:45 a.m. Wednesday, Sept. 23. A six-story apartment building at 1484 Montgomery Avenue, the Bronx. A two-alarm fire broke out, amNY reported. One person died. Others were injured.

A 31-year-old man jumped from a window to escape, according to the FDNY. He was taken to Jacobi Hospital in critical but stable condition. At least 10 other people were hurt, fire officials said, along with four firefighters. After the fire was under control, responders found an unidentified adult. That person was pronounced dead at the scene, amNY reported.
The fire spread quickly to nearby apartments and the roof, FDNY Deputy Chief Andrew Holzmaier said, according to amNY. It moved mostly through bathroom walls, where pipes and electrical wiring run.
A vehicle blocking a hydrant in front of the building slowed the response, the FDNY said. The Bureau of Fire Prevention issued summonses totaling $4,000 and towed the vehicle, amNY reported.
A man was seen in a hallway with an incendiary device before the fire, sources told amNY. Fire marshals have not determined the cause. No arrests had been reported. The investigation is ongoing.

man-shot-dead-in-downtown-brooklyn-park-.title: Man, 24, Fatally Shot in Downtown Brooklyn Park; Two Men Sought
man-shot-dead-in-downtown-brooklyn-park-.dek: A 24-year-old Brownsville man was shot to death in McLaughlin Park after an argument with two men. They remain at large, amNY reported.
body: Tuesday afternoon, Sept. 22. McLaughlin Park, Downtown Brooklyn. A 24-year-old man from Brownsville was shot and killed, according to police sources cited by amNY. Police are searching for two men seen confronting him.

The NYPD received a 911 call at about 2:07 p.m., the outlet reported. Officers from the 84th Precinct found the man with gunshot wounds to the stomach. EMS took him to NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital in critical condition. He was pronounced dead there.
Witnesses told investigators the man had been seen arguing with two other men before the shooting, according to the report. What the argument was about was not clear.

One of the two men was last seen in a gray Nike Tech suit, carrying a black backpack, police said. The other wore a green Nike Tech suit. After the shooting they reportedly ran north on Flatbush Avenue, then east toward Concord Street.

No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, according to amNY. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

teen-shot-dead-in-queens-gunman-fled-on-.title: Teen Fatally Shot in Arverne; Gunman Fled on Victim's Scooter, Sources Say
teen-shot-dead-in-queens-gunman-fled-on-.dek: A 14-year-old boy was shot during an attempted robbery behind the Ocean Bay Apartments in Arverne. Police released an image of the suspect, amNY reported.
body: Just after 5:30 p.m. Monday, Sept. 21. Behind the Ocean Bay Apartments, 51-24 Beach Channel Drive, Arverne, Queens. A 14-year-old boy was shot and killed, according to police sources cited by amNY. The outlet reported that he lived a few blocks away.
The boy was riding his scooter, police said. A man approached and tried to rob him. The boy resisted. The gunman shot him in the lower back, according to police.

The shooter then took the boy's scooter and fled east on Beach 52nd Street, police said. He was last seen riding east along Norton Avenue. Sources confirmed to the outlet that the scooter was used to get away.
The shooting was reported to the 101st Precinct. EMS took the boy to Cohen Children's Medical Center. He was pronounced dead there, according to the report.

On Tuesday the NYPD released an image of the suspect. He is described as a male with a dark complexion, last seen in a black hooded sweatshirt, black and gray pants, and red and white sneakers. No arrests had been made as of publication. The investigation was continuing. Through Sept. 20, the 101st Precinct had recorded five homicides this year, up from three a year earlier, amNY reported. Tips go to Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

mother-and-son-shot-inside-bronx-laundro.title: Mother and Son Shot While Doing Laundry in Allerton
mother-and-son-shot-inside-bronx-laundro.dek: A 37-year-old woman and her 17-year-old son were each shot in the leg inside a laundromat on Astor Avenue in the Bronx, amNY reported.
body: About 7:15 p.m. Monday, Sept. 21. The Astor Laundromat, 760 Astor Avenue, in the Allerton section of the Bronx. A 37-year-old woman and her 17-year-old son were shot while washing clothes, according to police sources cited by amNY.
Officers from the 49th Precinct answered a 911 call reporting gunfire inside the laundromat, police said. They found the mother and son each with a gunshot wound to the right leg.
Officers gave first aid until EMS arrived, the outlet reported. EMS took both to Jacobi Hospital. They were listed in stable condition.

Police did not immediately have a description of the gunman. Investigators were looking into whether the two were the intended targets or were hit by gunfire aimed at someone else, according to the report. As of Tuesday morning, the motive was not known.

No arrests had been made as of publication, amNY reported. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X, where tips are kept confidential.

man-beaten-and-slashed-in-unprovoked-bro.title: Man, 60, Beaten and Slashed Outside Kingsbridge Apartment Building
man-beaten-and-slashed-in-unprovoked-bro.dek: A 60-year-old man was struck from behind and slashed with a box cutter outside a Sedgwick Avenue building in the Bronx, police sources told amNY.
body: About 8:43 a.m. Monday, Sept. 21. Outside an apartment building at 2710 Sedgwick Avenue, in the Kingsbridge section of the Bronx. A 60-year-old man was beaten and slashed, according to police sources cited by amNY. Police described the attack as unprovoked.

The man was standing outside the building talking with another person, law enforcement sources said. The attacker came up from behind and struck him with an unknown blunt object. Then he pulled out a box cutter and cut the man on the neck, police said. He ran off in an unknown direction.

Officers from the 50th Precinct and EMS responded. Paramedics took the man to St. Barnabas Hospital with a head injury and a cut on the left side of his neck. He was listed in stable condition, according to the report.
The attacker was last seen in a green baseball cap, a blue coat and light-colored pants, police said.

No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, the outlet reported. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit a tip at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

14-year-old-critically-wounded-in-far-ro.title: 14-Year-Old Boy Critically Wounded in Far Rockaway Shooting
14-year-old-critically-wounded-in-far-ro.dek: A 14-year-old boy was shot in the back near Beach Channel Drive on Monday afternoon. Police were seeking a male who fled on a scooter, amNY reported.
body: About 3:36 p.m. Monday, Sept. 21. Near 51-24 Beach Channel Drive, Far Rockaway, Queens. A 14-year-old boy was shot in the back, according to police sources cited by amNY.

The boy was walking in the area when shots were fired, police sources said. Officers from the 101st Precinct responded. EMS took him to Cohen Children's Medical Center. The outlet described him as critically wounded. It reported that he was listed in serious condition.
Investigators were looking into whether the boy was shot during a possible attempt to rob him of his scooter, according to police sources.
Authorities said they wanted to question a male last seen leaving on a scooter. He wore a black sweatshirt and white shorts.

No arrests had been made. The investigation was continuing, according to the report. Police asked the public to stay away from the area while they worked the scene. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

hubspot-660-layoffs-dharmesh-shah-apolog.title: HubSpot Cuts 660 Jobs; Cofounder Apologizes for His LinkedIn Farewell
hubspot-660-layoffs-dharmesh-shah-apolog.dek: Cambridge software company HubSpot announced about 660 layoffs, roughly 7 percent of its workforce. Cofounder Dharmesh Shah later apologized for a LinkedIn post about the cuts that critics called cold.
body: On Tuesday, Oct. 6, nearly 660 people at HubSpot, the marketing-software company headquartered in Cambridge, were told their jobs were being eliminated.

Chief executive Yamini Rangan announced the cuts in a letter to employees, Boston.com reported. They amount to about 7 percent of the workforce. A week later, one of the company's two founders was apologizing in public for the way he had said goodbye.
## The Cuts

HubSpot was founded in 2006 by Brian Halligan and Dharmesh Shah, then MIT graduate students. It has more than 9,000 employees, about 306,000 customers and 15 offices worldwide, according to Boston.com. The company did not say how many of the eliminated jobs are in Massachusetts.

Rangan presented the layoffs as a reorganization, not belt-tightening. She wrote that the move is not simply about cutting costs, Boston.com reported. She also said the reductions were not driven by efficiency gains from new automation technology. In a year when that explanation is common, she went out of her way to rule it out.

What is changing, she said, is what HubSpot sells. The company is moving from building software that helps customers grow to delivering results for them directly. That shift, she wrote, is transforming its products, its pricing and how it serves customers.

Product teams will be reorganized around customer outcomes instead of around the company's individual software products, known internally as Hubs, according to Boston.com. HubSpot also plans to remove layers of management.

Departing employees will receive 20 weeks of base pay plus one more week for each year of service, capped at 30 weeks. They will also get health benefits and six months of career-transition services. They can keep their company laptops and home-office equipment.
## The Post

Shah is HubSpot's cofounder and chief technology officer, and he has more than 1.2 million followers on LinkedIn. After the layoffs he posted a brief note, the Boston Globe reported. It thanked departing employees for helping build the company and wished them well in their next chapter.
The response divided. Some commenters called the message impersonal and out of touch, according to the Globe. Others said it was good that he had acknowledged the layoffs at all.
## The Apology

Shah then added an apology to the post. He wrote that he was sincerely sorry his original message had been curt and insensitive, the Globe reported. He said he had wanted to express gratitude publicly but had failed to acknowledge the pain and uncertainty of losing a job.
> "I should have showed the people who helped build HubSpot more care and empathy." — Dharmesh Shah

Before HubSpot, Shah founded the software company Pyramid Digital Solutions, which was acquired in 2005, according to the Globe. He started HubSpot the following year. He has written widely about startups and marketing.
HubSpot did not say when the job cuts would take effect, according to Boston.com.

nvidia-reportedly-pushes-tsmc-3nm-base-d.title: Nvidia Reportedly Asks Memory Makers to Use TSMC 3nm Base Dies for Custom HBM
nvidia-reportedly-pushes-tsmc-3nm-base-d.dek: Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to build the base dies for its custom high-bandwidth memory on TSMC's 3nm process, according to reports cited by TrendForce.
body: Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to use TSMC's 3nm process for the base dies of NVHBM, TrendForce reported Oct. 19, citing Seoul Economic Daily. NVHBM is the custom high-bandwidth memory product Nvidia unveiled in August.

Samsung's Device Solutions division, which oversees its foundry business, agreed to the requirement after an internal review, according to the report. Nvidia wants to standardize production across its suppliers, the report said, to keep memory performance consistent and make product validation simpler. TrendForce did not say that any of the companies had confirmed the arrangement.

The stakes sit in a small layer of silicon. The custom base die holds a memory controller that has traditionally lived in the GPU, and that requires advanced logic manufacturing, according to TrendForce. Nvidia has said NVHBM offers up to 30% more memory bandwidth and 15% lower memory power use than standard HBM4E, the outlet reported. Industry estimates cited by Seoul Economic Daily put TSMC's 3nm yields above 90%. Samsung Foundry's 2nm process is at about 60%.

Samsung is also validating NVHBM base die production on its own 2nm process, according to the report, as a backup if TSMC capacity runs short. Samsung and TSMC compete for major foundry customers such as Qualcomm and Tesla, TrendForce noted.

On its Oct. 15 earnings call, TSMC said 3nm capacity is tight, according to TrendForce. The node accounted for 33% of third-quarter wafer sales. Chairman and CEO C.C. Wei announced plans for another 3nm fab in Tainan, targeted for mass production in the first half of 2028, the outlet reported, citing Economic Daily News.

samsung-and-tsmc-team-up-on-custom-memor.title: Samsung and TSMC Team Up on Custom Memory Chips for Nvidia
samsung-and-tsmc-team-up-on-custom-memor.dek: Samsung is working with its rival TSMC on the base die for Nvidia's custom high-bandwidth memory, the Seoul Economic Daily reported.
body: Samsung Electronics is working with TSMC, its foundry rival, on a key part of Nvidia's custom high-bandwidth memory, known as NVHBM, the Seoul Economic Daily reported Oct. 18, citing industry sources.

Nvidia is co-designing the memory's base die with both companies, according to the report. The base die is the logic layer at the bottom of the memory stack. Nvidia wants it made on TSMC's 3-nanometer process. Industry estimates put that process's yield above 90%. Samsung's comparable 2-nanometer process is at roughly 60%.

The design takes the memory controller off the graphics processor and puts it on the base die, the newspaper said. That frees space for more computing circuits. It reported that NVHBM can widen memory bandwidth by up to 30% and cut power use by 15% compared with standard HBM4E.

All of this happens against a projected shortage. UBS estimates next year's demand for high-bandwidth memory at about 61.5 billion gigabits, up 91%, according to the report. New shipments are expected to reach 54.6 billion gigabits. TSMC has said it will add 3-nanometer production lines in Taiwan, Arizona and Japan.

Samsung is also validating base die production on its own 2-nanometer process in case TSMC's capacity runs short, an unnamed industry official told the newspaper. The two companies last worked together about four years ago, on TSMC's packaging technology for AI chips.

deepseek-releases-updated-v4-1-flash-mod.title: DeepSeek Releases Updated V4.1-Flash Model
deepseek-releases-updated-v4-1-flash-mod.dek: The Chinese company said the update shortens task execution time and output length, SiliconANGLE reported.
body: Chinese artificial intelligence developer DeepSeek released an updated version of its V4.1-Flash model on Oct. 18, SiliconANGLE reported. The original launched on Sept. 10, about five weeks earlier.
The model card on Hugging Face calls DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 a minor update that reduces task execution time and output length, according to the report. DeepSeek did not say by how much.

In DeepSeek's own testing, the update resolved 77% of tasks on the DeepSWE v1.1 software engineering benchmark, SiliconANGLE said. The September version resolved 74.2%. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 scored 74% on that test, but it led on seven of the 11 benchmarks DeepSeek published.

DeepSeek also introduced search and page-fetch interfaces for agent software, according to the report, each priced at 75 cents per 1,000 successful requests. Calls made through DeepSeek's own Harness tool, Anthropic's Claude Code or OpenAI's Codex are free until Nov. 1.

The release follows a nearly five-hour API outage on Oct. 15, SiliconANGLE reported. Yicai Global counted it among DeepSeek's worst this year. The company apologized and issued credits to users. The updated model is available in DeepSeek's apps and through its API at unchanged prices. Its weights are published under the MIT license.

samsung-to-use-tsmc-for-base-die-in-nvid.title: Samsung to Use TSMC for Base Die in Nvidia's Custom HBM
samsung-to-use-tsmc-for-base-die-in-nvid.dek: Samsung will rely on TSMC's 3-nanometer process for part of Nvidia's custom high-bandwidth memory, Seoul Economic Daily reported, citing industry sources.
body: Samsung Electronics will use TSMC's 3-nanometer process to make the base die for Nvidia's custom high-bandwidth memory, known as NVHBM, according to an Oct. 18 report by Seoul Economic Daily citing industry sources. The paper called it the first manufacturing-stage partnership between the two chipmakers.

Until now, Samsung made both the core die and the base die for all of its HBM supply in-house, the report said. Nvidia asked its three NVHBM suppliers, Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, to use TSMC's 3nm process for the base die, according to the paper. It also asked them to standardize the core die on the sixth-generation DRAM process known as 1c. Nvidia said differing manufacturing methods make consistent performance difficult, the report said, and that standardization reduces validation work for each supplier. One customer is setting the terms for three suppliers at once.

NVHBM is based on the HBM4E architecture, the seventh generation of the technology, according to Seoul Economic Daily. Nvidia unveiled it in August. Samsung's Device Solutions division accepted Nvidia's request after an internal review, the paper reported.

For standard HBM, Samsung will keep its in-house approach, according to the report. It will use its own 4nm foundry process for the base die of HBM4 and HBM4E, and for custom HBM for other customers, including AMD.

The company is also checking whether it can produce the NVHBM base die at its own foundry, the paper said. An unnamed industry official described that as a hedge in case demand exceeds TSMC's capacity.

deepseek-pushes-out-updated-ai-model-it-.title: DeepSeek Releases Updated Model It Says Is Faster and Leaner
deepseek-pushes-out-updated-ai-model-it-.dek: The Chinese startup released V4.1-Flash-1017, a minor update it says scores better on benchmarks and finishes tasks faster.
body: Chinese startup DeepSeek released an updated version of its model on Saturday, Oct. 17, according to Bloomberg. It said the new version is faster and leaner than the last. The model, V4.1-Flash-1017, was announced in a series of posts on X, the outlet reported.

The company said the update offers stronger benchmark performance, faster task completion and shorter outputs, according to Bloomberg. It is available on the web, in DeepSeek's app and on its developer platform.

DeepSeek called the release a minor update to its earlier V4.1-Flash model, Bloomberg reported. A technical report the company posted on Hugging Face cites improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks and visual benchmarks. On the Humanity's Last Exam benchmark, the updated model scored in a range of 36.8 to 42.6, according to Bloomberg. V4.1-Flash scored 36.8 to 39.1.

The Hangzhou-based company competes with U.S. developers including Anthropic and OpenAI, and with Chinese rivals Moonshot and Z.ai, the outlet said. Earlier in the week, Bloomberg reported, DeepSeek had an outage of about five hours that left its servers unreachable. Some experts attributed it to insufficient computing resources.
The earlier V4.1-Flash came out in early September. It was priced low enough that shares of rivals including MiniMax, Z.ai and Alibaba fell in Hong Kong trading, according to Bloomberg.

microsoft-pulls-out-of-uk-data-center-de.title: Microsoft Pulls Out of UK Data Center Deal With Nscale, Report Says
microsoft-pulls-out-of-uk-data-center-de.dek: Microsoft has ended an agreement for an Nscale data center in Essex, England, Britain's Telegraph reported. The cloud provider had faced grid delays ahead of a planned IPO, according to Reuters.
body: Microsoft has withdrawn from a data center deal with Nscale, a British cloud computing provider, according to a Sunday report in Britain's Telegraph newspaper, as relayed by Reuters.

Microsoft is one of Nscale's two largest customers. It recently ended its agreement for a data center in Loughton, Essex, Reuters reported, citing the Telegraph. The newspaper did not say why. Microsoft declined to comment.
Nscale had faced repeated project delays, the Telegraph reported, according to Reuters. National grid officials told the company they did not expect to supply power to the site until the 2030s.

An Nscale spokesperson said the company's relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term, Reuters reported, and that the grid issue does not affect its other contracts. Nscale said it remains committed to the Loughton project and the U.K. It is exploring alternative power sources for that site and other expansion sites.

Nscale is an AI infrastructure company backed by Nvidia. It filed for a U.S. initial public offering last month, according to the report, and its prospectus lists Microsoft and Anthropic as expected major customers. It competes with CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe and Lambda. In about two and a half years it has grown its total contracted value from $100 million to more than $103 billion, Reuters said.

nvidia-ceo-says-coreweave-is-improving-a.title: Nvidia CEO Says CoreWeave Is Improving and Needs No Backstop
nvidia-ceo-says-coreweave-is-improving-a.dek: Jensen Huang played down concerns about the AI cloud provider on the same day its credit default swaps hit a record, The Next Web reported.
body: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said Thursday that CoreWeave's cost of capital is falling and that Nvidia does not need to backstop the AI cloud company, according to The Next Web. The outlet cited an interview Huang gave Bloomberg during a European trip.
Huang said CoreWeave's strength was improving every day, the outlet reported. He said he was optimistic.

Credit markets read it differently that same day. CoreWeave's five-year credit default swaps rose as much as 74.5 basis points to 1,194.5, a record intraday high according to ICE Data Services, The Next Web said. That level implied a more than 60% chance of default within five years. In June, the swaps had been at 452 basis points.

Nvidia is CoreWeave's second-largest shareholder, with a stake of about 10%, according to the report. It also sells the company the chips its business depends on. CoreWeave's total debt was about $30 billion in June, roughly triple the level a year earlier. It carries a speculative-grade credit rating. Its backlog reached $99.4 billion by July.

The Next Web also reported that Nvidia is said to be in talks to backstop $250 billion of OpenAI's data center financing. Neither company has confirmed it. Critics argue that Nvidia's investments in customers that then buy its hardware may inflate demand, the outlet said. Huang has called that idea ridiculous. The IMF and the Bank for International Settlements have flagged it as a systemic risk.

microsoft-ai-completes-pre-training-of-2.title: Microsoft AI Completes Pre-Training of 2.8 Trillion-Parameter MAI-Base-2
microsoft-ai-completes-pre-training-of-2.dek: Microsoft published technical details of its largest in-house base model and claimed large efficiency gains over a leading open model, Tech Times reported.
body: Microsoft AI has finished pre-training MAI-Base-2, a base model with 2.8 trillion parameters, according to Tech Times. On Oct. 15 the company published engineering details claiming it is far more compute-efficient than a leading open model.

The model was trained on 16,000 Nvidia GB200 chips over 38 days and finished pre-training in September, the company said, Tech Times reported. It uses a mixture-of-experts design, with about 80 billion parameters active for each token. It was trained on roughly 50 trillion tokens of data, about 18% of it combining images and text. Vision was built into the model from the start, not added later through a separate encoder.

Microsoft claimed its training recipe is 4.2 to 12.3 times more efficient in computing operations than that of DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base, the outlet said. Chief executive Mustafa Suleyman cited a 12-fold gain in a post on X. The company credited four changes, including a different optimizer and a method for routing data through the model without dropping tokens.

Tech Times noted that the efficiency figure is a projection based on scaling laws, not a direct comparison. Microsoft did not disclose confidence intervals for it. The actual training run used more total compute than DeepSeek's model. Microsoft said it spent the savings on building a larger model. Efficiency, in this telling, did not mean using less.

Post-training is still under way, according to the report. Microsoft has not released public weights, pricing or an availability date. It is positioning the model as an enterprise product through its Foundry platform, not an open release. It said work on a successor, MAI-Base-3, has begun.

tesla-unveils-long-delayed-roadster-with.title: Tesla Unveils Long-Delayed Roadster With SpaceX-Built Thrusters
tesla-unveils-long-delayed-roadster-with.dek: Elon Musk showed a redesigned second-generation Roadster that Tesla says it will build in 2028. He gave no price, TechCrunch reported.
body: Tesla unveiled its long-delayed second-generation Roadster on Oct. 15, according to TechCrunch. The redesigned sports car uses thrusters developed with SpaceX. Chief executive Elon Musk called it the best of the last of the human-driven cars.

At the event in Texas, the car used high-powered fans and thrusters to drive up an inverted ramp, spin and land, TechCrunch reported. It lifted itself over other Tesla vehicles while moving. Tesla showed it going from 0 to 60 mph in one second.

Musk said Tesla will build the car in 2028, the outlet said. He did not announce a price. The company plans three versions, all with about 300 miles of range and top speeds above 230 mph. Performance is a two-seat model. Thrust is a two-seat model with rear cold-gas thrusters. Rocket is a single-seat model with 10 thrusters. Reservations cost $50,000 for Performance and $250,000 for Thrust. Rocket is invite only.
The thrusters draw on 600 liters of rechargeable compressed air stored in carbon-fiber pressure vessels, Tesla engineering vice president Lars Moravy said, according to TechCrunch.

The Roadster was first shown in 2017. Early buyers put down $50,000 deposits then. Its reveal was pushed back several times, most recently from Oct. 1 because of weather, the outlet reported. Musk has described the car as a halo product that may not move the needle much on revenue.
